description: Class talk from Living Server, rewritten: each line is said only by the class it is about.

lines.text: At this level my Armsman has like three styles and I mash all of them.
Getting the first real set of plate is a big day for an Armsman.
An Armsman at this level is mostly a tin can with a sword.
Polearm Armsman life, slow swings and even bigger hits.
I see a Paladin chanting and wonder what it is like to bring more than a sword.
Crossbow on an Armsman is for pulling and nothing else, and it does that fine.
At this level an Armsman is mostly a wall with opinions.
Parry, shield and plate. Some fights I do not even notice the add hitting me.
The Armsman way: taunt it, stand there, trust the healer.
No class takes a beating like an Armsman and I will hear no argument.
Soloing on an Armsman is slow but steady, plate forgives a lot.
An Armsman's repair bill could feed a small village.
Early on a Paladin is just a tank who hums a lot.
One chant at a time for now, twisting can wait.
Chant twisting finally makes sense, my fingers hurt.
Paladin in a group: chants up, taunt up, nobody thanks the chants.
The endurance chant is why the whole group can keep swinging.
Twisting four chants and still swinging feels like juggling.
Two handed Paladin damage is better than people say. Not great, but better.
Paladins do not run out of endurance, we hand it out.
Plate, a big sword and a choir of chants. The Paladin dress code.
I love my chants but some days I envy the Armsman polearm.
A group with a Paladin just lasts longer, endurance and health regen add up.
Solo Paladin is slow, chants cannot kill things for you.
Dual wield at this level misses a lot, but when both swings land it is great.
Starting Mercenary, still figuring out which hand does what.
Evade and parry stacking on my Mercenary, half the hits just go past me now.
Mercenary solo is a gamble, sometimes the yellow dies, sometimes I do.
Chain armor and two swords, the Mercenary uniform.
At this point a Mercenary in chain does more damage than half the realm.
Two weapons, no shield, no apologies.
The class is called Mercenary but nobody ever pays me.
Mercenary envy is real, I look at Reaver lifetaps every time I get low.
Nothing beats watching both hands crit at once on a Mercenary.
A Mercenary in a group just needs a target and a healer who likes them.
A young Reaver is just a fighter with a flail and dreams.
Low level Reaver, the flex skill is still pretty sad.
Soulrending lifetaps keep me going when the healer runs dry.
The PBAE on a Reaver makes every pull a little exciting.
Reaver in a group means the healer has one less person to worry about.
High level Reaver: lifetap, pulse, smile.
The flex reach on a Reaver still feels like cheating.
Reavers look evil but we just want a group.
I see Paladins get groups and remind myself Reavers exist too.
Reaver solo is underrated, the lifetaps make up for no healer.
Black chain and a spiked flail, the Reaver look is unmatched.
Early Scout is all missing, the bow spec comes later.
First time something walked right past me while I was hidden, Scouts are fun.
Hidden on a hill with a longbow, waiting. That is the Scout life.
A Scout with a good bow and high bow spec is a scary thing.
A shield on a Scout really saves lives, mine mostly.
Scouts always get to the loot last, we stand so far back.
Scout envy: watching an Infiltrator walk up and stab things without a worry.
A Scout in a group pulls, shoots and stays out of the way.
Albion archery is the best in the land, I will say that to any hunter or ranger.
Low level Infiltrator, mostly stealthing past things I cannot kill yet.
Applying poisons before every fight, the Infiltrator ritual.
Backstab, follow up, vanish, the Infiltrator way.
Infiltrator solo at this level is slow and careful, and I like careful.
This high an Infiltrator is mostly patience and one great moment.
High crit strike on an Infiltrator, one good opener ends most fights.
Infiltrators do not lose fights, we just never start the ones we would lose.
Minstrels stealth too and still get invited, Infiltrator envy is real.
Nobody asks for an Infiltrator in a hunting group and I do not blame them.
Leather and two short blades, light and quick.
Nobody in Albion moves quieter than an Infiltrator, that is a fact.
My charmed pet broke again, Minstrel problems.
Mez on a Minstrel is the most useful thing I do and nobody sees it.
High level Minstrel is half tank half jukebox.
Minstrels have stealth too, people forget that.
I do envy Bards a little, they get heals with their songs.
Chain armor and a lute, the Minstrel is better armored than people think.
Speed to the frontier, courtesy of your local Minstrel.
Low level Cleric, mostly smite until someone needs me.
The first rez on a Cleric is a big moment, I still remember mine.
Rejuv Cleric in a group, eyes on the health bars the whole time.
A Cleric's buffs are half the reason the tank lives, nobody says it.
High level Cleric means raising the same person three times a night.
Smite spec at this level is serious damage, nobody believes it until they see it.
The tank dies, the Cleric gets blamed.
Clerics in chain, Wizards in robes, I know who got the better deal.
Solo Cleric is slow but I can heal myself through anything.
Albion Clerics, holding up every group in the realm.
Half my friends list is people I raised once.
Friar at this level is just a monk with a stick.
Staff in one hand, heals in the other, the Friar way.
Friar in a group: heal, swing, heal again.
Solo Friar is really strong, a staff and a self heal go far.
High level Friar staff crits surprise people, even me.
Friars take a vow of poverty and my repair bill keeps it.
Friar envy: watching a Cleric walk around in chain while I bonk things in robes.
Friar evade and parry let me soak a pull in robes.
Two classes in one robe, the Friar never gets bored.
Still hunting for a good quarterstaff, Friar problems.
Low level Wizard, one bolt and then run.
Medding between every pull is the Wizard life at this level.
Fire Wizard at this level, most fights end before melee.
A Wizard in cloth learns to respect every add, one death at a time.
A PBAE Wizard in a good dungeon group is a beautiful thing.
A Wizard's answer to everything is more fire.
Wizard envy: Theurgists get pets, I get a robe and a prayer.
Solo Wizard is fine if you pull carefully and keep a quickcast ready.
Nothing in Albion hits harder at range than a Wizard on a good day.
A good focus staff matters more than any robe on a Wizard.
Theurgist at this level, pets everywhere and no idea who they are attacking.
Earth Theurgist pets keep things busy while I cast.
My pet count on a Theurgist is never the same twice.
High level Theurgist pet spam can lock down a whole camp.
Theurgist pets have no loyalty, but there are always more.
Theurgist envy: Cabalists get one pet that listens, I get a dozen that never do.
Solo Theurgist is safe as long as the pets keep coming.
Robes and a cloud of elementals, that is the Theurgist look.
Sorcerer at this level is mostly mez and hope.
Mind Sorcerer mez lands, the group lives.
Body Sorcerer debuffs make every fight shorter and nobody says thanks.
High level Sorcerer, the crowd control is rock solid.
A Sorcerer solos well when the pet behaves, so almost never.
A Sorcerer in a group watches the adds more than the target.
Albion Sorcerers are the reason half the fights go our way.
My simulacrum is my best friend at this level.
Cabalist damage over time ticking on a yellow while my pet tanks, peaceful.
Matter Cabalist damage over time plus a stubborn pet, solid solo.
My simulacrum has more personality than most groups.
Cabalist envy: Sorcerers get the group spots, we get blank looks.
Cloth, a focus staff and a pet built by hand, that is Cabalist life.
A Cabalist in a group is mostly damage over time and quiet.
A patient Cabalist outlasts anything, that is the whole secret.
Low level Necromancer, the pet does everything and I watch.
Being the shade still feels strange, Necromancer life.
Painworking Necromancer, steady drains and a patient pet.
High level Necromancer pet tanks yellows without a complaint.
Deathsight Necromancer is a whole different class at this level.
Necromancers are not evil, we just keep odd hours.
Necromancer envy is real, everyone wants the Cleric and nobody asks for the dead fellow.
The dead serve Albion too, quietly.
Necromancer solo is the best in Albion, I stand by it.
Young Warrior, big shield, tiny plan, lots of heart.
Warrior in a group: taunt, block, repeat.
Thrown weapons on a Warrior are perfect for pulling, nobody believes me.
At this level hardly anything gets past my Warrior's shield.
Hammer Warrior here, every weapon is fine if you block enough.
Warriors do not need magic, we have the healer.
Warrior envy: Berserkers get all the damage, we get the bruises.
Midgard Warriors have held the line since the first winter.
Solo Warrior is slow, chain keeps me alive but kills take forever.
A low level Thane is a warrior who found a spellbook.
Stormcalling crits on a Thane still make me grin.
Thane in a group: pull with lightning, tank with a hammer, out of power by the second add.
At this level a Thane nukes like a caster and tanks like a warrior.
Thanes bring the storm to every fight, the healers complain about the noise.
Thane envy: warriors do not worry about power.
Chain, a big hammer and a head full of thunder.
Solo Thane is not bad, nuke it in and finish it with the hammer.
How much stormcalling is enough on a Thane, I go back and forth?
Skald at this level, speed and a sword, not much else.
Skald songs on, everyone runs faster.
Skald nukes land harder than people expect.
A Skald nuke and a big two handed swing ends most fights fast.
Skalds sing badly but the speed is real.
Skald envy: healers get thanked, Skalds get asked for speed.
A Midgard group without a Skald just takes the long way everywhere.
Young Berserker, swinging two axes and hoping.
Berserk frenzy on a Berserker is amazing until the healer looks away.
Left axe spec on a Berserker, every swing counts.
High level Berserker damage is silly, the defense less so.
Berserkers have one plan and it involves axes.
Berserker envy: warriors and Thanes get to carry a shield.
Solo Berserker is quick until it is not, and then it is a long run back.
Nothing in Midgard swings faster than a Berserker in a frenzy.
Savage at this level, punching things and loving it.
Savage self buffs eat health but the extra speed is worth it.
Hand to hand Savage, fast claws and a lot of bandages.
High level Savage swings so fast the healer cannot keep up.
We Savages hurt ourselves to hurt others harder, it makes sense after a while.
Savage envy: everyone knows the Berserkers and hardly anyone remembers us.
Savages are the newest fighters in Midgard and the angriest.
Good claws are hard to find, Savage problems.
Stealthed on a hill with a composite bow, watching. Hunter life.
Hunter and pet soloing yellows is the best.
At this level a Hunter with a good pet can handle most camps.
I trust my pet more than my group, Hunter habit.
Hunter envy: rangers and scouts get the archery talk, we get asked about the pet.
A Hunter's pet is the only groupmate that never asks for loot.
Midgard Hunters can do it all, ask anyone.
Feeding the pet and buying arrows, Hunter money disappears.
Young Shadowblade, still learning where to stand.
Poisons on, hidden, waiting, the Shadowblade life.
Left axe Shadowblade, both weapons and a lot of crits.
Shadowblade solo is careful but rewarding.
High level Shadowblade opening chains end fights before they start.
A Shadowblade's best friend is the shadow behind the tank.
Shadowblade envy: healers get the invites first, every time.
Nobody asks for a Shadowblade in a hunting group, I stopped minding.
Midgard Shadowblades can wait longer than any stealther alive.
Low level Healer means heal, sit, repeat.
Group heals landing right on time is the best feeling.
High level Healer heals are huge, the power never keeps up though.
A mending Healer at this level can keep anyone standing through anything.
Healer rule one: never stand next to the puller.
Healer envy: Berserkers get to swing axes and I count health bars.
Solo Healer is a slow grind, hit and heal, hit and heal.
Midgard Healers might be the best of any realm, I will say it again.
Low level Shaman, little damage over time and lots of patience.
Cave Shaman damage over time ticking on everything.
Shaman buffs on the tank, a heal on standby, ready.
A high level Shaman heals, buffs and rots things all at once.
Shamans carry the smell of the cave, you get used to it.
Shaman envy: healers get the big group heals, we get the smell.
A group with a Shaman hits harder, the buffs do that.
Shaman solo is solid, damage over time it and wait.
Young Runemaster, one nuke then a long med.
Darkness Runemaster nukes land big.
High level Runemaster nukes carry fights, the robe does not save me.
Runemasters carve runes for fun, then nuke things from range.
Runemaster envy: Spiritmasters have someone to hide behind, I have a prayer.
Solo Runemaster is about pulling one at a time, a single add is the end.
Runemasters are the biggest nukes Midgard has.
Low level Spiritmaster, my spirit tanks while I cast.
Summoning Spiritmaster, the spirit tanks better than some warriors.
Spiritmaster soloing feels cozy behind a good pet.
High level Spiritmaster, the pet hits harder than I do.
Spiritmasters argue with spirits for a living, nothing odd about it.
Spiritmaster envy: Bonedancers get a whole army of pets, I get a single spirit.
A Spiritmaster with a healthy pet can handle anything blue.
Cloth robes, a staff and a spirit at my shoulder.
Young Bonedancer, one skeleton and big plans.
Commander out, subpets following, Bonedancer life.
Bonedancer lifetaps keep me going after the pets go down.
High level Bonedancer pets hold the pull by themselves.
A Bonedancer never eats alone, the skeletons are good company.
Spiritmasters only lose one pet at a time, Bonedancers lose the whole army.
Bonedancers are Midgard's newest casters and probably the strangest.
Cloth, a staff and a clattering escort.
Young Hero, a big spear and no idea.
Celtic spear reach on a Hero is lovely on pulls.
High level Hero, shield spec and no regrets.
The class is called Hero and still nobody cheers when I walk in.
Hero envy: Blademasters get the damage, heroes get the healer's attention.
Heroes of Hibernia never step back from a pull.
Solo Hero is slow but safe, shield up and patience.
Young Champion, still figuring out what valor even does.
Champion debuffs land and suddenly the group hits harder.
Large weapons Champion here, debuff first, swing second.
High level Champion, the valor spells turn yellows into blues.
Champions are the unsung heroes, the heroes take the credit.
Champion envy: Blademasters get the credit for my debuffs.
A group with a Champion just kills faster, everyone knows it.
Solo Champion is decent, debuffs then swing.
Young Blademaster, two swords and little aim.
Celtic dual crits on a Blademaster never get old.
Blademaster in a group, stick to the tank and hit with both hands.
High level Blademaster damage is unreal on a good pull.
Blademasters solve every problem with two blades.
Blademaster envy: heroes get shields, Blademasters get a second sword.
Solo Blademaster is quick kills and long rests.
Nothing in Hibernia spins prettier than a Blademaster.
Young Warden, heals and a sword, not great at either.
Warden heals keep the tank standing while I swing.
Nurture buffs on a Warden make the whole group stronger.
High level Warden can heal and tank at once.
A Warden does a bit of everything and nobody says thanks.
Warden envy: Druids get pets and bigger heals, we get a shield.
A group with a Warden just dies less, simple as that.
Solo Warden is solid, swing and heal and swing again.
Young Druid, my pet tanks and I heal.
Druid group heals land and everyone breathes again.
High level Druid, my heals are solid, the pet is handy.
Druids talk to trees for fun.
Druid envy: Bards and wardens get to swing a sword, I stand back.
Druid solo with the pet is comfy, buff it and watch.
Hibernian Druids, the best heals in the land.
Bard mez holds the adds down while the group fights.
The Bard kit: speed, heals, mez and a lute.
High level Bard, twisting songs like it is nothing.
Bards do everything, a little badly, but in tune.
Bard envy: Druids get bigger heals, Bards get songs.
A group with a Bard never walks, Hibernia's best taxi.
Young Ranger, a short bow and a lot of misses.
Hidden Ranger with a recurve, waiting, quiet.
Pathfinding buffs on a Ranger matter more than people think.
Rangers love nature until it bites back.
Ranger envy: scouts get shields and I get a recurve.
Ranger solo is smooth, arrows first, blades when it arrives.
Hibernian Rangers move quieter than any archer in the land.
Young Nightshade, hiding more than fighting.
Nightshade opener lands and the rest is easy.
High level Nightshade, critical strike and a little patience, that is all.
Nightshades prefer the dark, daylight makes us nervous.
Nightshade envy: rangers take the group spots.
Nobody asks for a Nightshade in hunting, we stay hidden either way.
Hibernia's Nightshades are the quietest blades in the land.
Young Eldritch, bolt, run, bolt again.
Void Eldritch damage hits so hard the tank barely gets a swing in.
Mana Eldritch PBAE is risky but so much fun.
High level Eldritch, big nukes and no armor.
People say Eldritches look creepy, we just stare a lot.
Eldritch envy: Enchanters have pets to hide behind, I get a robe.
Solo Eldritch is fine until an add shows up.
Hibernian Eldritch nukes are the best anywhere.
Young Enchanter, the pet tanks and I buff.
Enchanter PBAE with a pet tanking is unfair.
Enchanter buffs make the group hit harder.
High level Enchanter, the pet holds and everything dies around me.
Enchanters are polite, the pets less so.
Ench envy: Eldritches nuke harder at range, but we have friends.
Solo ench with a good pet feels cozy.
Hibernian Enchanters carry more groups than people realize.
Young Mentalist, a little healing, a little mez, lots of medding.
Mentalist mez holds the adds down nicely.
Mentalist in a group: backup heals, mez and nukes when it is quiet.
High level Mentalist mez holds most rooms with no fuss.
Mentalists read minds, and most monsters think about food.
Mentalist envy: Druids get bigger heals, Eldritches get bigger nukes.
A Mentalist does a bit of everything, Hibernia needs that.
Solo Mentalist is fine thanks to a mez and a self heal.
Young Animist, one shroom and a lot of hope.
Animist turrets everywhere, nothing knows what hit it.
Arboreal path Animist here, still learning the turrets.
High level Animist turrets shred anything that walks up.
Animists garden for a living, the garden just bites.
Animist envy: Enchanters get pets that follow, mine stay put.
No other class turns a clearing into a garden that bites.
Solo Animist is mostly setting turrets before the pull.
Young Valewalker, a big scythe and no idea what to do with it.
Scythe swings on a Valewalker hit hard.
A Valewalker in cloth up front makes every healer nervous.
High level Valewalker, buffs and a heavy scythe, strange but fun.
Valewalkers carry a scythe and nobody knows why.
Valewalker envy: heroes get real armor, Valewalkers get cloth.
Valewalkers are the oddest fighters in Hibernia and proud of it.
Solo Valewalker is better than you think.
After all these levels in plate I still flinch when a caster looks my way.
Soloing on the Armsman, one pull at a time and no rush.
Still picking which chant to keep up, health regen wins for now.
Out soloing on the Mercenary, every pull is a coin toss.
A Mercenary with a good off hand weapon is a happy Mercenary.
People see a Reaver and assume we are trouble, we usually are.
Reaver at this level is all about picking the right moment to pulse.
Soloing on the Scout, lots of walking backwards.
Scouts see the fight first and loot it last.
An Infiltrator's favorite sound is the second crit.
Minstrels are the only fighters who bring a lute to a sword fight.
High level Minstrel mez is the reason half my groups survive.
Keeping an eye on everyone's health, Cleric habits.
A Cleric who smites is a Cleric who gets yelled at, I do it anyway.
A Friar in the back row is a Friar wasting a staff.
First staff style on the Friar and I felt unstoppable.
Soloing on the Wizard, quickcast on standby, nerves on standby too.
Every Wizard has a story about the add that came from nowhere.
A Theurgist's pets are loud, messy and loyal for about thirty seconds.
Out soloing on the Theurgist, pets doing the hard part.
Mez timers are the only clock a Sorcerer really watches.
Still learning which mez lasts how long on the Sorcerer.
A Cabalist rebuilds the pet more often than anyone wants to know.
Soloing on the Cabalist, damage over time ticking, nothing in a hurry.
A Necromancer's real body never sees combat, and I like it that way.
High level Necromancer, the pet is scarier than anything we fight.
A Warrior's shield has more dents than my bank has coins.
Soloing on the Warrior, slow kills but nothing scary.
A Thane's favorite sound is thunder right before the hammer lands.
First stormcalling spell on the Thane, I used it on everything.
High level Skald, the songs run on habit and the nukes still hit hard.
A Berserker counts health in seconds, not points.
Out soloing on the Berserker, fast kills and faster rests.
A Savage with full buffs is a beautiful, short lived thing.
High level Savage, the buffs are huge and so is the health bill.
Soloing with the pet, the Hunter's way.
A Hunter's pet gets more praise than the Hunter, as it should.
Out solo on the Shadowblade, stealthed and in no rush.
Healers notice who stands in the wrong place, every time.
High level Healer, the big group heal is worth every point of power.
Shamans buff the group and get thanked by the tank, sometimes.
Soloing on the Shaman, damage over time up and a heal ready.
First few levels on the Runemaster, every bolt feels like a big deal.
Spiritmasters never feel alone, the spirit sees to that.
Out solo with the spirit, it does the hard part.
Bonedancers clatter, there is no sneaking up on anything.
High level Bonedancer, the army does the fighting and I do the counting.
A Hero's shield has seen more fights than most of Hibernia.
Soloing on the Hero, slow and steady.
Champions make everyone else look good, that is the whole point.
High level Champion, the debuffs land and the group feels unstoppable.
A Blademaster without a second weapon is just sad.
Soloing on the Blademaster, both blades busy.
Wardens get yelled at for not healing and for not tanking, sometimes at once.
First heal on the Warden saved my own life, felt good.
Keeping the group healed and the pet out of the way, Druid life.
A Druid's pet is the only friend who never complains.
High level Bard, the mez is the real reason groups want me.
Soloing on the Ranger, arrows and patience.
Rangers notice tracks nobody else sees, or we pretend to.
A Nightshade's best friend is a slow moving target.
High level Nightshade, the opener is everything.
Out solo on the Eldritch, pulling one at a time.
An Enchanter's buffs are the gift nobody remembers to thank.
Early Enchanter levels are mostly nuking and hoping.
Mentalists get blamed when the mez breaks and forgotten when it holds.
Soloing on the Mentalist, mez one and kill the other.
Animists plant first and ask questions later.
Out solo on the Animist, turrets planted and waiting.
Valewalkers get looks in town, the scythe does that.
High level Valewalker, the scythe finally feels right.
Anyone want to duo? I talk a lot but I heal all right.
Ugh, out of arrows mid fight.
Every day in this plate and I creak like an old gate.
A Paladin never runs, he walks with purpose.
Heh, Cleric life: everyone loves you right up until they die.
Smite Cleric or rez Cleric, the group always wants the other one.
A Friar does not need plate, a Friar needs faith and a good staff.
Nothing in the realm hits like a Wizard with a full power bar.
The academy taught me fire and ice and very little about running.
Theurgist life, three pets out and none of them listen.
A Sorcerer in a good group is a mez machine, the Hibs hate it.
Infiltrator life, nobody sees you and nobody thanks you.
An Albion longbow sings when you let it go, no other realm has that.
Minstrels carry this realm on speed songs and charm.
The church still asks about my flail. I do not answer.
Mercenary means I fight for Albion and for the loot, mostly Albion.
Healing Albs is a calling, nobody says thanks after a bad pull.
The academy and the guilds argue, but every Alb caster agrees the Hibs are worse.
Nothing beats fresh polish on my plate before a long hunt.
A Warrior's shield has more stories than any Skald.
Thor hears me when I call, the Albs hear it too.
A Skald without a fight to sing about is just a loud Dwarf.
Heh, when the frenzy hits, I forget my own name.
Savage life is simple, fists up, face forward.
Healer life: everyone yells my name right before they die.
Shamans cure what we can and curse what we cannot.
Runes never lie, they just hit very very hard.
My pet looks like a nightmare and it is my best friend.
My skeletons follow me better than most groups do.
The casters of Midgard get no respect until the Albs start falling over.
Nothing beats a fresh edge on my axe before a long hunt.
A Hero's shield is the oldest tree in any forest.
Champion life: debuff them, then hit them with a sword.
Two blades, one Blademaster, and not much left of the Alb.
My pet is more polite than most Mids I have met.
A Ranger's arrow does not miss, it just has a long way to go.
Nightshade life, you never see me, you only feel it.
Eldritch life, burn hard and pray the tank holds.
My pet has better armor than the whole group.
Mentalists do three jobs and get thanked for none.
My mushrooms do the fighting, I just water them.
A Valewalker cuts through Albs like summer wheat.
The path casters of Hibernia argue, but every one of us agrees the Albs are worse.
Nothing beats a fresh edge on my weapon before a long hunt.
Polearm or two handed? I keep going back and forth.
Armsman life: stand in front, get hit, be happy.
Nothing feels better than a big polearm style landing.
Chant twisting is harder than it looks.
Paladin endurance chant, the group's best friend.
Dual wield Mercenary, more swings more fun.
Mercenary tip: evade is your friend, train it.
Flex is weird at first but the reach is nice.
Soulrending feels like cheating sometimes.
Still figuring out Reaver, anyone have advice?
Longbow and patience, that is the whole class.
People complain about Scout range, they should try aiming.
Quiet night, just me and my envenom.
Crit strike or envenom first, cannot decide.
Smite Cleric or rejuv, the eternal question.
Cleric life: heal, rez, get blamed, repeat.
Staff Friar here, I heal and I hit, both badly some nights.
Nobody expects the Friar to tank.
Fire Wizard, I solve problems from far away.
Earth or fire, every Wizard argues about it.
Wind Theurgist, the art of throwing pets at things.
Mind Sorcerer tip: mez first, ask questions later.
Cabalist damage over time stack up nicely if you are patient.
My simulacrum takes more hits than I do, as intended.
Necromancer tip: the pet is you, you are the pet.
Painworking Necromancer, the slow kill is the best kill.
Warrior: shield up, face first, no regrets.
Throwing weapons on a Warrior, more useful than it sounds.
Stormcalling Thane, I bring the thunder.
Thane life: half caster, half tank, all fun.
Skald speed is the best gift in Midgard.
Battlesongs up, everyone run faster.
Berserker, two axes, no plan.
Left axe Berserker, the berserk style never gets old.
Savage buffs cost me health but look at those numbers.
Hand to hand Savage, punching things since level five.
Hunter and pet, best duo in the realm.
Composite bow at range, spear up close, I like options.
Shadowblade, stealthed and waiting.
Mending Healer, keeping groups alive since forever.
Healer life: everyone loves you until the group wipes.
Cave Shaman, diseases and damage over time, everything rots eventually.
Mending Shaman, the group's quiet backbone.
Runemaster damage is no joke when it lands.
Darkness or suppression Runemaster? Asking for my build.
Spiritmaster pet is tankier than half my groups.
Summoning Spiritmaster, I let the spirit do the talking.
